title: Sense of Privacy and Territoriality as a Function of Spatial Layout in University Public Spaces
research_question: How does spatial layout in university public spaces affect students' sense of territoriality and privacy?

participants.description: University students from Yarmouk University, Jordan. Nearly all majors of study, with nearly half males and half females.
participants.recruitment: Students were randomly selected from Yarmouk University and voluntarily agreed to participate in face-to-face interviews and fill out questionnaires.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: Five manipulated 8x5 inch colored photographs of an outdoor public space at Yarmouk University, representing different spatial layouts:
Layout A: Outdoor space subdivided by both horizontal and semi-vertical elements.
Layout B: Outdoor space with no subdivisions (open enclosure).
Layout C: Outdoor space occupied by a central vertical element.
Layout D: Outdoor space occupied by a central horizontal element.
Layout E: Outdoor space subdivided by a central kiosk (attractive for pedestrians).

measures.instrument: Self-report 5-point Likert scale (8 items, Factor 2, α=0.88)
Self-report 5-point Likert scale (10 items, Factor 1, α=0.84)

findings.antecedent: Sense of territoriality
findings.mechanism: Territoriality is an important mechanism for attaining privacy, as it allows individuals to control access to their space.
findings.quote: main effect for territoriality on scores of sense of privacy (F (1,149) = 240.815, P<0.0001). The correlation was reported to be R = 0.787

mechanisms: Spatial layout influences sense of privacy and territoriality by providing visual separation and control over interaction.
Vertical spatial elements have a greater impact than horizontal ones in promoting privacy and territoriality.
The ability to control interaction with others is crucial for both privacy and territoriality.
Territoriality serves as a mechanism for achieving privacy.
implementation_implications: Designers and landscapers should improve environmental quality in university public spaces by stressing positive spatial design aspects that promote sense of territoriality and privacy.
Suitable landscape structures in public spaces can impact and encourage friendship formation.
Making boundaries and enclosures for private shared group spaces avoids conflict and clears out ambiguity, strengthening group membership.
Consider pattern, layers, and exposure to pedestrian traffic in spatial layout.

limitations: The study was geographically limited to one outdoor open space at the Yarmouk University campus in Irbid, Jordan.
More quasi-experimental research studies are needed at other campuses to assess the relationship between spatial layout and healthy interactions among groups of university students.
